condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The closest structural analog verapamil has absolute oral bioavailability of 22% (95% CI 17–29%) after a 120 mg oral tablet in fasted healthy volunteers versus IV (C24), a point estimate at/above the 20% threshold.
Norverapamil sustained-release records report F of 49±14% fasted and 34±12% fed (C09, C21), supporting that verapamil-like scaffolds can exceed 20%.

L5 verapamil gut-wall records show high jejunal permeability and minor P-gp contribution (C69, C71, C80), while other records show P-gp efflux and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism can be inhibited to increase exposure (C72, C79, C75); these are mechanistic and do not provide a direct low-F outcome for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability data exist for the query molecule.
No query-specific oral AUC/Cmax, permeability, solubility, efflux, or metabolism measurements are available; L3-L5 records are for verapamil or unrelated molecules.
The effect of the cyclic 1,3-dithiane 1,1,3,3-tetraoxide modification on verapamil-like scaffold F is unquantified.
Verapamil F point estimate (22%) is close to the 20% threshold with CI 17–29%, so threshold classification is sensitive to analog transferability.
L5 efflux/metabolism evidence is mixed (high permeability/minor P-gp vs efflux-limited permeability and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism), and its net effect on query F is unclear.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F≥20%) because the most transferable direct endpoint evidence, verapamil absolute oral bioavailability of 22% in fasted volunteers (C24) and norverapamil SR F of 49%/34% (C09, C21), supports the threshold; L5 gut-wall efflux/metabolism records are mechanistic, mixed, and do not provide an affirmative low-F outcome for the query. The low physicochemical prior is uncertain and insufficient to override the close-analog experimental outcome; unresolved uncertainty is reflected in low confidence.
